Simulate an omics dataset with known quality problems

simulate_omics.Rd

Generates a synthetic samples-by-features matrix on a log-abundance scale, with correlated feature clusters, a chosen pattern of missing values and, optionally, planted quality problems whose identity is returned alongside the data. Because the truth is known, the output can be used to check what quality_control() removes and keeps under a given set of thresholds, to compare settings (for example fast = TRUE against fast = FALSE), and as example data for tests and tutorials.

Usage

simulate_omics(
  n,
  p,
  n_factors = NULL,
  frac_clustered = 0.3,
  loading_range = c(0.6, 0.9),
  miss_rate = 0.1,
  miss_mech = c("lod", "mcar", "mixed", "none"),
  complete_frac = 0,
  plant = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  equal_rates = FALSE,
  miss_ignores_shift = FALSE,
  as_omiprep = FALSE
)

Arguments

n

integer, the number of samples (rows).

p

integer, the number of features (columns).

n_factors

integer, the number of latent factors behind the correlated feature clusters. NULL (default) uses one factor per five clustered features.

frac_clustered

numeric (0 to 1), the share of features that load on a latent factor. The remaining features are independent.

loading_range

numeric vector of length 2, the range from which each clustered feature's loading on its factor is drawn. Values must lie between 0 and 1.

miss_rate

numeric (0 to <1), the target share of missing values, as the mean of the per-feature rates.

miss_mech

character, how values go missing: "lod" (default), the lowest values of each feature, as when they fall below a lower limit of detection; "mcar", values missing completely at random; "mixed", half of each feature's missing values by each mechanism; "none", no missing values.

complete_frac

numeric (0 to 1), the share of features that are left with no missing values from miss_mech.

plant

named list of problems to plant, or NULL (default) for none. See the section "Planted problems".

seed

a single integer, or NULL (default). If supplied, set.seed() is called with it so the same call returns the same data. This changes the random number state of the session.

equal_rates

logical. FALSE (default): per-feature missingness rates vary around miss_rate (beta-distributed, at most 0.75), as in real data. Some features labelled "clean" will then exceed a missingness threshold by themselves (about 1 in 8 features is at least 20% missing when miss_rate = 0.1). TRUE: every feature has exactly miss_rate, so only planted features have high missingness.

miss_ignores_shift

logical. FALSE (default): values below the detection limit are chosen after the dilution and outlier shifts, so a sample shifted down also gains missing values. TRUE: they are chosen on the unshifted values, so diluted and outlier samples have the same missingness as other samples and differ only in their values.

as_omiprep

logical. FALSE (default) returns a list; TRUE returns an Omiprep() object built from it.

Value

If as_omiprep = FALSE, a list with three elements that can be passed directly to Omiprep():

  • data: numeric matrix, samples in rows and features in columns, with row and column names.

  • samples: data frame with columns sample_id, batch (a random label, "b1" or "b2", unrelated to the data) and truth, the label of what was planted in the sample ("clean" if nothing).

  • features: data frame with columns feature_id, platform (constant), truth, the label of what was planted in the feature ("clean" if nothing), and cluster_factor, the latent factor a clustered feature loads on (NA for independent features).

If as_omiprep = TRUE, an Omiprep object holding the same data, with the tables above in its samples and features properties.

Details

The data are built in this order:

  1. Base data. Every value starts as an independent standard normal draw. The first frac_clustered of the features are then assigned to one of n_factors latent factors and mixed with it (loading drawn uniformly from loading_range), which gives clusters of correlated features. Each feature is then given its own mean (uniform on 8 to 14) and standard deviation (uniform on 0.4 to 1.5).

  2. Planted problems and biological controls (see the plant argument), applied to the complete data. Each sample or feature receives at most one of them.

  3. Missing values, according to miss_mech and miss_rate.

  4. Extra missing values for planted poor features and failed samples.

Nothing is planted unless requested: with plant = NULL every sample and feature is labelled "clean". The label of what was planted is returned in the truth column of the sample and feature tables, so it stays with the data when they are passed to Omiprep() and through quality_control(). Note that the QC report treats truth like any other sample or feature variable, so it will appear among the candidate batch variables.

Planted problems (plant)

plant is a named list. Each *_frac entry is the share (0 to 1) of samples or features given that problem; all default to 0. Entries not supplied keep their default.

Technical problems, which quality control is expected to remove:

  • dilution_frac, dilution_shift (default 1): diluted or concentrated samples. Every feature of the sample is shifted up or down (direction chosen at random per sample) by dilution_shift feature standard deviations. Truth label "tech_dilution".

  • outlier_frac, outlier_shift (default 1): outlier samples. Each is shifted along one random direction across the features, shared by the planted samples and not present in the rest of the data, scaled by outlier_shift feature standard deviations. Truth label "tech_outlier".

  • failed_frac, failed_miss (default NULL): failed samples, given extra values missing at random. failed_miss is the share of features set missing; if NULL it is drawn per sample from 0.5 to 0.9. Truth label "tech_failed".

  • poor_feat_frac, poor_miss (default NULL), poor_mech (default "random"): poorly detected features, given extra missing values. poor_miss is the share of samples set missing; if NULL it is drawn per feature from 0.5 to 0.95. With poor_mech = "random" the extra values are missing at random; with "lod" the lowest values still observed are set missing, as for a feature that is often below its detection limit. Truth label "tech_poor_feature".

  • trunc_frac, trunc_quantile (default 0.6): features capped at an upper limit. Values above the trunc_quantile quantile of the feature are set to that quantile, which gives a left-skewed feature. Truth label "tech_truncated".

Biological controls, which quality control is expected to keep:

  • bio_subgroup_frac, bio_subgroup_shift (default 2): a subgroup of samples shifted by bio_subgroup_shift feature standard deviations on the features of the first latent factor only. Requires frac_clustered > 0. Truth label "bio_subgroup".

  • bio_tsa_frac, bio_tsa_shift (default 0.5): a subgroup of samples with higher abundance, shifted by bio_tsa_shift feature standard deviations on a random 40% of the features. Truth label "bio_tsa".

  • rare_frac: features with a rare effect. A random 8% of samples are shifted up by 3 feature standard deviations, which gives a right-skewed feature. Truth label "bio_rare_effect".

Examples

# 200 samples by 200 features, 10% of each feature missing, with a few failed samples and
# poorly detected features planted
sim <- simulate_omics(
  n = 200, p = 200, miss_rate = 0.10, equal_rates = TRUE, seed = 1,
  plant = list(failed_frac = 0.02, poor_feat_frac = 0.05)
)
dim(sim$data)
#> [1] 200 200
table(sim$samples$truth)
#> 
#>       clean tech_failed 
#>         196           4 
table(sim$features$truth)
#> 
#>             clean tech_poor_feature 
#>               190                10 

# the same data as an Omiprep object; the truth labels are kept in the sample and feature tables
m <- simulate_omics(
  n = 200, p = 200, miss_rate = 0.10, equal_rates = TRUE, seed = 1, as_omiprep = TRUE,
  plant = list(failed_frac = 0.02, poor_feat_frac = 0.05)
)
table(m@samples$truth)
#> 
#>       clean tech_failed 
#>         196           4 

# run quality control and compare what was excluded with what was planted
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
m <- quality_control(m, source_layer = "input", cores = 1)
excluded_samples  <- unique(unlist(m@exclusions$samples))
excluded_features <- unique(unlist(m@exclusions$features))
table(truth = m@samples$truth,  excluded = m@samples$sample_id   %in% excluded_samples)
table(truth = m@features$truth, excluded = m@features$feature_id %in% excluded_features)
} # }
